title: Job 34
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu continued, ² "Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who know. ³ For the ear tests words just as the tongue tastes food. ⁴ Let us discern together what is right; let us learn among ourselves what is good. ⁵ For Job has said, 'I am innocent, and God has denied me justice.'

⁶ 'Should I lie about my rights? My wound is incurable though I have done nothing wrong.' ⁷ Is there another man like Job, who drinks up insults like water, ⁸ who keeps company with evildoers and walks in the way of the wicked? ⁹ For he says, 'A man gains nothing by trying to please God.' ¹⁰ So listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God to do evil, from the Almighty to commit wrong.

¹¹ He repays everyone for what they have done; he brings on each person what their conduct deserves. ¹² It is unthinkable that God would do wrong or that the Almighty would pervert justice. ¹³ Who put him in charge of the earth? Who appointed him over all creation? ¹⁴ If he chose to take back his spirit and breath, ¹⁵ every living thing would perish together, and humanity would return to dust.

¹⁶ "If you have any understanding, then hear this; listen to what I say. ¹⁷ Can a ruler who hates justice be in power? Will you condemn the one who is supremely just? ¹⁸ Is he not the one who says to kings, 'You are worthless,' and to nobles, 'You are wicked'? ¹⁹ How much less does he show favor to princes, or treat the rich better than the poor — for all of them are made by his hands. ²⁰ They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; the mighty are brought down — not by human hands.

²¹ For his eyes are on every person's path; he sees every step they take. ²² There is no darkness deep enough to hide the evildoer from him. ²³ He does not set a time for any person to come before him in judgment. ²⁴ Without inquiry he shatters the mighty and puts others in their place. ²⁵ He knows what they are doing; he sweeps them away in the night and they are crushed.

²⁶ He strikes them down for their wickedness, openly, in plain sight, ²⁷ because they turned away from following him and had no regard for any of his ways. ²⁸ They caused the cry of the poor to rise up to him, so that he heard the cry of the afflicted. ²⁹ When he is silent, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he governs both nations and individuals, ³⁰ to keep the godless from ruling and from ensnaring the people.

³¹ Suppose someone says to God, 'I have suffered punishment; I will sin no more. ³² Show me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.' ³³ Should God reward you on your terms, when you reject him? The choice belongs to you, not to me — so say what you know. ³⁴ Men of understanding will tell me, and every wise man who listens to me will agree: ³⁵ 'Job speaks without knowledge; his words have no insight.'
³⁶ I wish that Job would be tested to the limit for answering like a wicked man. ³⁷ For to his sin he adds rebellion; he defies us and speaks more and more against God."
